# Plan rules

## 1. One active plan

At any moment, the current active plan is the complete set of non-archived content under:

```text
inputs/obtained/
```

There is only one active plan.

A plan may contain one document or several documents.

## 2. Archive the previous plan as one unit

Before generating a new plan, `/plan` MUST move all active content from:

```text
inputs/obtained/
```

excluding:

```text
inputs/obtained/archived/
```

into one new directory:

```text
inputs/obtained/archived/plan-YYYYMMDDhhmmss/
```

A single timestamp MUST identify the complete archived plan generation.

## 3. Timestamp format

The archived plan directory name is:

```text
plan-YYYYMMDDhhmmss
```

The timestamp:

- uses local execution time;
- contains exactly 14 decimal digits;
- contains no separators.

Example:

```text
plan-20260817004330
```

## 4. Preserve archived plan contents

Files archived as part of the previous plan MUST retain:

- their original filenames;
- their contents;
- their relative structure below `inputs/obtained/`.

Unlike the generic `/archive <document>` command, `/plan` archives the previous plan as a complete directory snapshot.

## 5. Never overwrite an archived plan

If:

```text
inputs/obtained/archived/plan-YYYYMMDDhhmmss/
```

already exists, `/plan` MUST NOT overwrite it.

The operation must fail clearly.

## 6. Generate the minimum coherent document set

There is no required number of plan documents.

The planner SHOULD prefer the smallest number of documents that preserves clear semantic boundaries.

Examples of legitimate separate concerns may include:

- architecture or structure;
- implementation sequence;
- acceptance criteria;
- migration;
- testing;
- deployment.

These are examples, not mandatory filenames or sections.

## 7. No arbitrary document-length rule

IASI MUST NOT impose a fixed maximum number of words, pages, headings or tokens for plan documents.

A document being large is a signal to reconsider cohesion, not an automatic reason to split it.

## 8. Scope is authoritative

The plan MUST remain inside the scope established by active inputs.

If an input states:

```text
For now, only create the project skeleton.
```

the plan MUST NOT include implementation of later product functionality.

Out-of-scope work SHOULD be made explicit when doing so helps prevent accidental expansion.

## 9. Planning may expose missing information

If `/plan` discovers that the work cannot be planned without making a material unsupported decision, it MUST stop and report the missing information.

It MUST NOT hide the gap by inventing a choice.

## 10. Obtained means derived

Documents generated by `/plan` belong to:

```text
inputs/obtained/
```

because they are knowledge derived by IASI from other active inputs.

They are not implementation outputs or external reports.

They re-enter the IASI input model and are subject to `/validate`.

## 11. Archived plans are historical

Everything below:

```text
inputs/obtained/archived/
```

is historical.

Archived plans MUST NOT participate in:

- planning;
- validation;
- contradiction detection;
- active input fingerprints;
- later execution decisions.

## 12. Plan generation changes validation freshness

Generating a new plan changes the active input set.

Therefore any validation performed before `/plan` cannot authorize execution based on the newly generated plan.

A new `/validate` is required after successful planning.
